data.name: Jogesh
data.gender_notes: Jogesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Jogesh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jagat' which means 'world' and 'Ish' which means 'lord'. The name Jogesh signifies the one who is the lord of the earth. The name Jogesh carries the meaning “Lord of the earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jogesh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine presence and control over the physical world.
data.etymology: Jogesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jogesh total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jogesh is of Hindu origin and holds a significant cultural impact for Hindus as it symbolizes power and control over the material world. It is a name often given to boys who are expected to grow up to be strong and influential figures in their community.
data.spiritual_significance: Jogesh represents the divine presence of God on earth. The name signifies that the individual bearing the name is a representative of the divine and is responsible for upholding spiritual values and maintaining harmony in the world around them.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jogesh: Embodiment of devotion and determination on the spiritual path. Name derived from the Sanskrit words 'Joga' (discipline) and 'Ish' (God).

historical_references.reference: Jogesh Chandra Chatterji was a noted Indian historian, born on 24 June 1897 in Kolkata, British India. He was the first professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta.
Jogesh Mukherjee was a Shankaracharya of the Advaita order of Hindu monasticism, born on 11 September 1915. He was the head of the Shankaracharya lineage at Puri, Odisha, from 1967 to 1994.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Jogesh is of Hindu origin, meaning 'God is graceful'. In modern times, people with this name have made a mark in various fields. On Twitter, Jogesh Mukherjee is a scholar and educator, regularly sharing insightful articles on technology and trends in education.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Krishna Jogesh in Kathmandu, Nepal attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Jogesh, which means "Lord of the earth". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
